newsitem.title: USA: Dlr starts mixed in U.S., bland G7 lifts dlr/yen.
newsitem.headline: Dlr starts mixed in U.S., bland G7 lifts dlr/yen.

text.p: Dollar/yen opened solidly, vaulting 115 overnight after a weekend summit of the Group of Seven (G7) nations yielded only a bland warning on Japan's trade surplus and an agreement to cooperate in foreign exchange markets.
The dollar backed off against the mark, however, giving mark/yen a leg up to resistance at 67.00 overnight.

"There was no statement, really, out of the G7, just that they would cooperate in FX. This has given (a) rise to dollar/yen," said Susan Stearns, a director of foreign exchange at Bank of Montreal in New York.
"But what we are really describing is a cross trade, because the yen has come off and the mark is bid," Stearns continued.

The dollar jumped to 115.67 yen overnight -- its highest in almost two weeks -- after the leaders of Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Canada, Japan and the United States issued a joint statement at the conclusion of the Denver gathering.
Dollar/yen eased a bit in Europe, opening at 115.30/40 in New York, up from 114.80/90 at Friday's close. The dollar opened at 1.7210/20 marks, down from 1.7285/90.

In the end, the G7 -- which this year invited Russia to all but one monetary meeting -- gave traders what they expected, agreeing Japan needs to spur strong domestic-led economic growth and avoid a significant increase in its trade surplus.
To these ends Japan also has the objective to put in place broader structural reforms and deregulation to revitalize its economy, the leaders said.
"Nothing really came out of G7 that surprised us," said Seth Garrett, chief dealer at Credit Suisse First Boston.
Traders said they expected Japanese exporters to offer dollars in the high 115 yen area. Buy orders should be found between 114.50 and 115 yen, they said.
In dollar/mark, stop-loss sell orders are expected below technical support at 1.72.
Before taking a hit right before the open, dollar/mark got some support from sterling/mark, which extended its rally to a 59-month high at 2.8700 on Monday, dealers said.
"Sterling/mark achieved (its highest) since July '92 and that is on the back of continued expectations of rate hikes from the Bank of England," Stearns said.
Cable opened at $1.6625/35, up from $1.6555/65, then quickly rose to a 5-month high at $1.6667.
The dollar rose to Canadian $1.3893/98 from C$1.3885/90.
The Australian dollar opened at $0.7503/08, near its $0.7506/11 close on Friday.
